lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: creating inequalities in one variable

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Item A costs $15 each and item B costs $23 each. You may spend at most $210 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 130 litres and is filling at 9 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 211 litres?
A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.
Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.
Report 4.3, because the model is exact.
Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $175 call-out fee plus $18 per hour. A job cost $409 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = 2bh − 4 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: Item A costs $10 each and item B costs $28 each. You may spend at most $130 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A tank holds 110 litres and is filling at 13 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 175 litres?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A model gives a required side length of −6 metres. How should this solution be interpreted?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
